column3: The Hebrew repeats “here” with building and preparing; BSB states the location once.
The Hebrew says “on the altar,” without an explicit “each”; BSB specifies “on each altar.”
The Hebrew gives “Stand by your burnt offering, and let me go”; BSB adds “here” and makes the departure a “while I am gone” clause.
The Hebrew names Balaam in the meeting clause and leaves the following speaker unnamed; BSB uses “him” first and then names Balaam. “Each” is also supplied in its altar description.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he returned “to him” and introduces the scene with “behold”; BSB names Balak and gives the scene as a relative clause.
The Hebrew leaves the oracle speaker unnamed and contains no separate “he said” inside Balak’s quoted request; BSB supplies Balaam’s name and adds “he said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular collective pronouns for the people; BSB uses plural “them” and “themselves.”
The Hebrew says “let my soul die” and ends with singular “like his”; BSB says “let me die” and plural “like theirs.”
The Hebrew emphasizes blessing by repeating the verb; BSB says “only blessed,” without preserving the repetition.
The Hebrew leaves the answering speaker unnamed; BSB supplies “Balaam.”
The Hebrew says the people’s “edge,” without explicitly naming a camp; BSB specifies “the outskirts of their camp.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed and says “on the altar”; BSB supplies Balak’s name and “each altar.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker and the one encountered unnamed; BSB supplies “Balaam” and “the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he “came to him”; BSB says he “returned to Balak.”
The Hebrew leaves the oracle speaker unnamed; BSB supplies “Balaam.”
The Hebrew pairs “said” and “spoken” with doing and establishing the word; BSB uses “speak” and the more specific “promise,” with “act” and “fulfill.”
The Hebrew has no explicit noun for a command in “I have received to bless”; BSB supplies “a command to bless.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “his God,” “with him,” and “in him”; BSB uses plural “their God,” “with them,” and “among them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks what God has done without an explicit adjective “great”; BSB adds “great things.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective verbs for the people and says they will not “lie down”; BSB uses plural subjects and “not resting.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the outcome may be “straight in the eyes of God”; BSB says it may “please God.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly addresses Balak and repeats “here”; BSB omits the addressee and gives the location once.
The Hebrew says “on the altar,” without an explicit “each”; BSB specifies “on each altar.”
